case_name: Sussex County Planning & Zoning Commission v. Smokey Hollow, LLC

issues.label: Certiorari jurisdiction and scope of review
issues.why: The court must confirm certiorari is the proper vehicle and define the limited scope of certiorari review versus statutory appeal.

issues.label: Failure to exhaust statutory appeal remedy
issues.why: Smokey Hollow could appeal to County Council under §99-39(A), raising whether it bypassed available remedies before seeking certiorari.

issues.label: Effect of no-appeal reconsideration provision
issues.why: Section 99-39(H) states there is no appeal from a reconsideration decision, potentially affecting reviewability of the conditions.

issues.label: Commission's authority to impose conditions
issues.why: Central dispute is whether the Commission may attach conditions beyond bare code compliance under §99-9(A).

issues.label: Standard for 'reasonable' conditions
issues.why: The court must articulate what makes a subdivision condition reasonable, which the Commission argues was underdeveloped.

issues.label: Approval of code-compliant plans
issues.why: Precedent may require approval of compliant plans subject only to reasonable adverse-impact-minimizing conditions.

issues.label: Whether Condition A minimizes adverse impacts
issues.why: The court must assess whether eliminating lot 64 addressed flooding/wetlands impacts or merely appeased neighbors.

issues.label: Deference to neighborhood opposition
issues.why: Whether public testimony alone can justify a condition or must be tied to legitimate land-use concerns.

issues.label: Substantial evidence for lot 64 findings
issues.why: The Commission's flooding, wetlands-crossing, and isolation findings must be supported by substantial record evidence.

issues.label: Conflict with legislative 30-foot setback
issues.why: Whether Condition A improperly overrides Council's legislative determination on perimeter setbacks.

issues.label: Setback versus buffer distinction
issues.why: The Code definitions differ; the court must determine whether the former §115-25F imposed a setback or a buffer.

issues.label: Applicability of cluster development standards
issues.why: Whether the Zoning Code's cluster development standards applied to Smokey Hollow's property affects Condition O's basis.

issues.label: Retroactivity/pending-application exemption of Ordinance 2852
issues.why: Whether the newly adopted average-buffer ordinance exempts pending applications and controls the buffer requirement.

issues.label: Which version of Code governs application
issues.why: The court must decide whether the former or amended buffer regulation applies to an application pending during amendment.

issues.label: Fixed versus average buffer authority
issues.why: Whether the Commission could impose a 25-foot fixed buffer when the applicable law contemplated an average buffer.

issues.label: Coastal Area environmental assessment requirements
issues.why: The property is in a Coastal Area with 50+ units, implicating §115-194.3 environmental assessment obligations relevant to conditions.

issues.label: Commission's failure to explain Condition O
issues.why: The Commission gave no reasoning for Condition O, raising whether the decision is reviewable and reasoned.

issues.label: Whether conditions exceed statutory police power
issues.why: Conditions must fall within the delegated zoning police power under the constitutional and statutory framework.

issues.label: Remedy of striking versus remand
issues.why: Whether the proper disposition is invalidating the conditions or remanding for the Commission to reconsider or explain.

issues.label: De novo review of legal errors
issues.why: The court must apply de novo review to legal questions while respecting factual findings supported by substantial evidence.

issues.label: Severability of conditions from approval
issues.why: Whether striking two conditions leaves the remaining 19 accepted conditions and the approval intact.
